branches.title: How many comparisons does that take?
branches.source: Each match keeps only the smaller value because the larger one cannot be the overall minimum—we already know a value smaller than it. Repeating this process keeps the overall minimum in the tournament until it is the last value remaining.

anchor.question: How many comparisons does that take?
anchor.snapshot: The learner is discussing a tournament tree that finds the minimum of eight numbers by comparing pairs and advancing the smaller value until one remains. A larger value is eliminated because a smaller value is already known, so it cannot be the overall minimum. Finding the minimum takes seven comparisons: four in the first round, two in the second, and one in the final. The learner now asks how many comparisons the process takes.
